title: AI caught my wrong-airport taxi
hook: AI was the reason I worked out I'd booked a taxi to the wrong airport.
summary: AI travel planning in Notion just saved my flight home.
body: AI travel planning in Notion just saved my flight home.

I connected my Notion OS to my itinerary, flights and bookings. At the bottom of the trip page it listed the usual checks (passport, packing), then added: "check your taxi on this day, I think you're going to the wrong airport."
It was right. My return taxi was booked to the wrong airport.
I don't let the agents action anything yet. They just flag it to me, and that was enough.
Comment "connect" and I'll send you how I set it up.
guide: Cover title: AI caught my wrong-airport taxi
Best time: Fri 9 Oct, 10:00 UK (Metricool top weekday slot on TikTok + Instagram)
This sets up an AI travel planner in Notion that reads your itinerary and bookings and flags problems for you to check. You need a Notion account, your trip details, and ChatGPT or Claude.
1. Create a trip page in Notion with a day-by-day plan, and add your flights, hotels, taxis and other bookings as linked entries or a database.
1. Paste in or link the booking confirmations, including airport names, terminals, dates and times for both outbound and return legs.
1. Connect an AI assistant to your Notion workspace, using Notion's own AI or the Notion connector in Claude or ChatGPT, so it can read the trip page and bookings.

1. Ask it to review the whole trip and add a "Things to check" section at the bottom of the page, covering documents, packing, and any booking that does not match another (for example, a taxi pick-up point against a flight's airport).
1. Tell it to flag only. It should write findings on the page and never rebook, cancel or message anyone.
1. Read the checklist a week before you travel and again the day before, and correct anything it got wrong.
1. Re-run the review whenever you add or change a booking, so the checks stay current.
Watch out: Keep the assistant read-only and flag-only; a flag you confirm yourself is safe, but an agent acting on a wrong guess can cause a real booking error.

```
You are helping me build an AI trip checker in Notion. I have a Notion workspace and a paid <ChatGPT / Claude> account.
Task: design a setup where the assistant reads my trip page and its linked bookings (<flights, hotels, taxis, other>) and writes a "Things to check" section at the bottom of the page.
Requirements:
- The assistant must have read access to the trip page and bookings, and write access only to that one section.
- It must never book, cancel, edit or send anything. It only flags.
- Each flag should name the booking, the date, what looks wrong, and why (for example, a taxi pick-up point that does not match the departure airport).
- Include the standard checks: passport validity, visas, packing, check-in times, and transfers between each leg.
- Say clearly when it is unsure, rather than guessing.
Return: a Notion page structure for my trip, the exact instructions to give the assistant, a short review prompt I can re-run after every change, and a step-by-step guide for connecting <Notion AI / Claude / ChatGPT> to my workspace. My trip: <destination and dates>.
```
